headline: President Biden canceled a 2017 executive order on expanding apprenticeship programs.
what_it_does: This order revokes Executive Order 13801, a 2017 order titled "Expanding Apprenticeships in America." That earlier order had set up a path for industry groups and others to create and recognize their own apprenticeship programs, separate from the existing government-registered system. With the 2017 order canceled, federal agencies are told to review and consider rolling back rules and policies that were based on it.

who_it_affects.group: Businesses, trade groups, and other organizations running industry-recognized apprenticeship programs
who_it_affects.how: The federal policy that supported their separate apprenticeship programs is withdrawn, and related rules may be rolled back.

who_it_affects.group: Workers in or considering apprenticeship programs
who_it_affects.how: The types of federally recognized apprenticeship programs open to them may change as agencies carry out the order.

who_it_affects.group: The U.S. Department of Labor and other federal agencies
who_it_affects.how: They must review and possibly undo rules and actions taken under the 2017 order.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed February 17, 2021; agency rule changes follow later.
